fixed-shooter.title: Shooter readiness and aiming
fixed-shooter.explanation: The source checks shooter speed, turret angle, hood angle and solution validity, then combines them. Shooter speed uses RPS; angles use radians.

trace.label: Read shooter speed
trace.explanation: The comparison uses a speed setpoint and a 4% tolerance.

trace.label: Check aim and validity
trace.explanation: The turret and hood checks are independent of the validity flag.

trace.label: Combine the checks
trace.explanation: All four flags must be true for this method to return true.

differences: The cited 254 robot has a turret; a chassis-heading gate in the fixed-shooter demo is a teaching adaptation, not this source method.
This method checks readiness; it does not itself feed a piece or demonstrate sensor freshness.

turret-shooter.title: Turret setpoint and IO
turret-shooter.explanation: The real hardware IO clamps the requested turret position in radians, converts units and gearing, and sends a position/velocity request to the controller.

trace.label: Clamp request
trace.explanation: Requested angle is bounded by configured turret position limits.

trace.label: Convert units
trace.explanation: Angle and velocity are converted to rotor rotations and geared units.

trace.label: Send position request
trace.explanation: The motor controller receives position and feedforward velocity.

differences: The excerpt clamps a requested angle; it does not establish cable-safe equivalent selection, homing, vision validation or collision monitoring.
The demo’s explicit fault and wrap-choice guards are separate hypothetical teaching behavior.

piece-handling.title: Coral intake branch ordering
piece-handling.explanation: During the straight coral collection case, back-sensor detection is checked before the two-front-sensor condition.

trace.label: Back sensor
trace.explanation: A tripped back range sensor yields the holding state.

trace.label: Front sensors
trace.explanation: If the back sensor is not tripped and both front sensors are tripped, the state indexes right faster.

trace.label: Otherwise collect
trace.explanation: If neither earlier condition matches, collection continues.

differences: The model may use beam-break or jam states to teach generic indexing; these source inputs are CAN range sensor booleans.
This excerpt does not establish sensor disconnect detection, a timeout, or confirmed successful scoring.

elevator-wrist.title: Elevator height and completion
elevator-wrist.explanation: The periodic method converts a stored position from inches to metres, while a command ends when the position reaches a supplied tolerance.

trace.label: Update height
trace.explanation: The robot state receives elevator height converted from inches to metres.

trace.label: Request position
trace.explanation: The method constructs a motion-magic position command.

trace.label: Check tolerance
trace.explanation: The command is bounded by a position comparison.

differences: This short source excerpt is an elevator example, not a full wrist, collision envelope, homing or timeout implementation.
Completion within tolerance is not evidence that a piece was placed or retained.

telescoping-arm.title: Shoulder and extension sequencing
telescoping-arm.explanation: In this branch, the arm requests shoulder angle and holds extension at zero until the measured shoulder is near its desired angle.

trace.label: Request shoulder angle
trace.explanation: The shoulder receives the wanted pose angle.

trace.label: Compare shoulder angle
trace.explanation: A tolerance in degrees determines which extension request to send.

trace.label: Choose extension
trace.explanation: The code sends zero if not near, otherwise the wanted extension in metres.

differences: This is one branch of a larger method; preceding branches and homing checks also affect behavior.
A zero extension target is a command, not proof of collision clearance or disabled-load retention.

drivetrain.title: Alliance and field-relative swerve input
drivetrain.explanation: The source applies alliance-dependent signs, scales velocities and makes field/robot frame conversions with a skew compensation factor.

trace.label: Alliance and scaling
trace.explanation: Translation signs depend on alliance; rotation is scaled separately.

trace.label: Compute skew compensation
trace.explanation: The angular speed contributes to a rotation compensation factor.

trace.label: Convert reference frames
trace.explanation: A field-relative conversion is followed by a robot-relative conversion using a compensated heading.

differences: The nested conversions return a field-relative result with compensation; do not describe this excerpt as only a direct field-to-robot output.
The educational differential-drive comparison, stale-sensor checks and model trajectories are not implemented in this excerpt.

climb-balance.title: Climber homing and cage candidate
climb-balance.explanation: The source idles requests other than HOME while unhomed and then uses current and roller-speed conditions to manage an intake/cage candidate state.

trace.label: Check homing
trace.explanation: Unhomed requests other than HOME return the idled state.

trace.label: Enable cage detection
trace.explanation: The check is enabled from a current and velocity condition.

trace.label: Assess cage candidate
trace.explanation: A retained candidate or subsequent velocity condition can lead to holding.

differences: This is a 2025 cage-intake/climber code branch, not a 2023 charge-station balance implementation.
A current/speed inference or software holding state does not prove hook engagement, mechanical retention or safe load support.
